mission.title: Caplet
mission.description: Obtain a sample of Zion's new red pill for analysis.

npc.say:
Blue and red, operative; and, if you mix them, a sickly purple.
Good night.
Oh my god oh my god oh my god...
Must I do this for you?
That is not in my instructions...
I could tell you what to do, but the Agent seems to like giving orders.

Danielle Wright is eccentric, but undeniably capable. We've monitored her closely since she left Zion, not only to watch for threats, but also to...examine any potentially worthwhile program she may develop. We've obtained a number of useful codes from her. The emergency jack-out system you use is the most widespread, I suppose, although that one she developed while still in Zion, and we had to obtain it from Zionite defectors.

What else? Oh, well, mostly just component subroutines for various technical uses in networks and so on... There was a certain one of her interface subroutines that I suspect may have been...studied for the Agent Pace project, but of course I didn't have access to that.

phase.briefing:
Operative, we have found that the Vauxton corporation known as "Wright Research" has been assisting Zion in developing a new red pill trace program that is immune to the exploit we used to gain data on their mainframe. Reports indicate that Danielle Wright, head of the corporation and a former Zion operative, has been carrying out the work personally. There are indications that this work continues, despite direct intervention by System forces against the Wright Research facility.
The Cypherites have contacted us, claiming to have further information regarding this matter. As you know, they are particularly interested--one might say "obsessed"--with the status of individual humans in the pod system. I am delegating you to meet with their leader, Cryptos.

enter.say:
Been a while since we had a chat with old Cryptos. I wonder if he's got his head straightened out yet? Gray seems to think he's okay...or, at least he doesn't worry about him being in charge as much as he does Veil.
I've got some redpill readings in there, and...yeah, there's Cryptos' scrambled signal.

talk.say:
Our sources within Zion bring word that Wright has already completed the code of the new red pill--even that limited quantities have started making their way to Zion extraction teams.
We have yet to encounter these teams in the field; they are still relatively quiet, as they have been for weeks. But this blissful respite may be coming to an end.

done.say: The new pills could already be hitting the street? Oh boy. Gray's gonna need to know about this.

phase.briefing:
If these new pills indeed exist, {player}, it is imperative that we obtain a sample for analysis.
The location indicated is a Wright fabrication facility, with higher than usual activity over the last twenty-four hours. Search the facility thoroughly.

enter.say: I've got some bluepill signals in there. Could be security, so keep an eye out.

objective.text: Get the access code from Denise Hoyos

done.say: A computer access code--could be useful.
You should be able to access that terminal now.

Oh, super.
She's thorough; I'll give her that.

near.say: Hey, finally someone who doesn't look like an ex-cop with a chip on their shoulder. Maybe there's something worthwhile in there.

phase.briefing:
We raised our monitoring level of known Zion "potential" extraction candidates as soon as we received your operator's report, operative.
Already we have indications of Zionites approaching one of these citizens: Austin Uris.
You are to eliminate the Zionite team, and confiscate any red pills they may be carrying.

enter.say:
We'd been ahead of Zion for a while, but that Wright chick pulled a pretty fast one. Time to catch back up.
I've got unregistered operative signals in there, and not one, but two bluepill signals.
That's weird. Usually they like to try getting them when they're alone.

objective.text: Get the red pill from the Zionite

done.say:
Okay. Let's call Gray and see what he wants us to do with it.
I'm sure he'll have someone else handy to take care of the...uh...mess there.

near.say: I'm reading a red pill code on that one. Can't tell for sure if it's one of the new type.

...
I'm sure he'll be fine. Yeah...

complete.say:
Huh. There's the extraction team's blue pill. We won't be needing that.
The Machines have their own way to calm people back down after they've gone through something like this. Zion just uses it to cover their tracks if an extraction doesn't go right--like this one.

phase.briefing:
Yes, a cleanup team will attend to that situation, operative.
Bring the pill to our lab for analysis. The coordinating officer is Agent West.

enter.say: That's the lab. No sign of trouble.

talk.say: You're slow, {player}. Insert the pill into the lab computer's analysis tray.

done.say: That's the nice thing about Agents: they're all so cheerful.

objective.text: Insert the red pill into the lab computer's analysis tray

done.say: Check the readout on that thing. Was it one of the new pill codes?

Ah, must have been one of the new ones, then. Good.
Hey-oh. You've got familiar company. I guess there's yet another Merv transmitter to find and shut down...

talk.say:
You may be interested to know, operative, that E Pluribus Neo plans to sabotage certain power lines running into the Machine city in the very near future. Full details can be found at data cluster 28090275.HNW.091, password "touche."
I would use my own Sentinels to deal with them, but I thought your masters might prefer to do it themselves.

done.say:
Why, that old son of a--
We'll just see what Gray thinks about this.

...projection is not subject to ballistic damage.
...
Please advise.

mission.finish:
Preliminary analysis of the pill code structure suggests that the author utilized data from the Zion mainframe to find, test, and fix our exploit. It is not usual for Zion to allow such access to their own operatives, much less a third party such as Danielle Wright. It is possible that Ms. Wright has her own means of accessing their mainframe. This...would be significant.
Ah... The other matter. Yes, the data reported by the General will be examined. It should not be difficult to determine whether or not it is merely another Merovingian ploy.
